title: Design an Internal RAG Assistant
interviewAnswer: Define document sources and permissions, ingestion/chunking, embeddings and indexes, retrieval/reranking, prompt construction, citations, evaluation, latency/cost and monitoring. Security boundaries matter as much as answer quality.
why: RAG system design combines document ingestion, retrieval, LLM behavior, evaluation, security and production architecture—ideal for AI engineering interviews.
intuition: Keep the source of truth outside the model. Retrieve only relevant evidence at query time, then ask the LLM to answer from that evidence with provenance.
deepDive: Clarify users, data sensitivity, freshness, query latency and citation requirements. Offline path: connectors → parsing → chunking → metadata → embeddings → vector/lexical indexes. Online path: auth → query transformation → retrieval/filtering → optional reranking → context assembly → generation → citations. Evaluate retrieval separately from generation. Add access-control filtering before context reaches the model.
workedExample: Internal engineering assistant: ingest approved PDFs/wiki pages, preserve document permissions in metadata, hybrid retrieve top-30, rerank to top-5, generate an answer with source citations, and refuse when evidence is insufficient.
commonMistakes: Retrieving documents a user is not authorized to see.
Assuming bigger context always improves answers.
Evaluating only final prose quality and not retrieval recall.
followUps: How do you choose chunk size?
How do you enforce document permissions?
production: Version ingestion/chunking/embedding configs, support incremental refresh/deletion, cache carefully, trace every retrieval/generation step, and define fallback behavior when retrieval confidence is low.

visual.title: Production RAG
visual.caption: A production RAG system needs ingestion, retrieval quality, security and evaluation—not just an LLM call.
